title: Saturday 19 December: arrive in Ho Chi Minh City
sub: Sleep in: Saigon (District 1). Dry, 24 to 32°C. Times are Vietnam time (Sydney is 4 hours ahead, Hong Kong 1 hour ahead).

stops.details: Direct (Vietnam Airlines or Vietjet). A 9 am Sydney departure is 5 am here and lands around 2 pm.
Airport Express to HKG, then about 2h45 flying. Choose a flight landing around 2 pm so you arrive together.
Whoever lands first waits in arrivals. E-visa check, SIM or eSIM.
Drop bags at the hotel, then pho somewhere busy and clean (Pho Hoa Pasteur).

commute.label: Grab to Pho Hoa Pasteur (about 150,000–200,000 VND)

stops.details: French colonial post office; Book Street is next door.
Stroll as the lights come on; coffee in the apartment-block cafés at No. 42.
stops.hours: Open all the time; liveliest after 5 pm

stops.details: Vietnamese dinner at Secret Garden (rooftop, popular, clean).
Saigon Saigon bar at the Caravelle for skyline views.

title: Sunday 20 December: Mekong Delta day trip

stops.details: Small-group or private Mekong tour picks you up at the hotel.
stops.cost: Small-group tour about US$35–70 (A$55–110), lunch included

stops.details: Sampan rides through coconut-palm canals, coconut-candy workshop, fruit orchard tasting.

commute.label: Tour bus to Ben Tre (85 km)

stops.details: Elephant-ear fish and local dishes at a garden restaurant, all cooked fresh.

stops.what: Bike or boat through the villages
stops.details: Easy cycle along the canals.
Shower and rest.
Banh Mi Huynh Hoa is busy and well known; take it back to the hotel or add a sit-down dinner nearby. You ride your own scooter on Phu Quoc instead (26 Dec).
Sydney morning calls from the hotel (9am Sydney is 5am here). Amy sleeps in.
Hotel breakfast or egg coffee nearby.
An easy morning before the afternoon sights.
The bubblegum-pink 1870s church on Hai Ba Trung, one of Saigon's most photographed spots. Photos from across the street; go inside only if the gate is open.
stops.hours: Gates often closed on Mondays; the pink front is the photo, from across the street

stops.details: Broken rice with grilled pork, a Saigon classic.
1960s palace frozen in time, with war-room bunkers underneath.
stops.hours: 8 am – 4:30 pm daily (last entry about 4 pm)

stops.details: Powerful and heavy.
Browse the stalls as the night market sets up outside.
stops.hours: Market about 7 am – 6 pm; night market outside after 6 pm

stops.details: Near Nguyen Hue.
An old apartment block at 42 Nguyen Hue with a different café or bar in almost every flat, lit up floor by floor. Pick one with a balcony over the street.

title: Tuesday 22 December: Saigon and the Cu Chi Tunnels

stops.details: Sydney morning calls from the hotel. Amy sleeps in.
Hotel breakfast or egg coffee nearby.

stops.what: Cholon: Thien Hau Temple and Binh Tay Market
stops.details: Giant spiral incense coils hang from the roof of this 1760 Chinese temple and fill it with smoke and light. Then a quick lunch around Binh Tay Market next door.

stops.what: Back at the hotel for the tour pickup
stops.details: The Cu Chi tour bus collects you at about 12:30 pm.
Half-day afternoon group tour to Ben Dinh: walk the jungle site, see the traps and hideouts, and crawl a short widened stretch of tunnel if you like. Wear clothes that can get dusty.

commute.label: Tour bus to Cu Chi (pickup at the hotel about 12:30 pm)

stops.cost: Half-day group tour about US$25–35 (A$40–55), entry included

stops.details: Shower and change.
Near Nguyen Hue. Pack for Phu Quoc.

title: Wednesday 23 December: fly to Phu Quoc
sub: Sleep in: Phu Quoc resort. Peak dry season, sunny, about 30°C.

stops.details: No meetings today. Leave bags at reception.
Collect bags on the way. Domestic terminal.
About 1 hour.

stops.what: Check in at the resort, pool
stops.details: Pick a resort with a big room or villa and laundry service.
Long Beach faces west for sunsets.
Easy first night.

title: Thursday 24 December: Christmas Eve on Phu Quoc
sub: Sleep in: Phu Quoc resort. Sunny, about 30°C. Scooter days start today: Matthew rides with Amy on the back until the morning of 27 Dec.

stops.details: No alarms today.

Rent one 125cc automatic for 3 days (24–26 Dec) from the resort desk or a shop on Tran Hung Dao. Check brakes, lights, tyres and the passenger footpegs, get two helmets with visors, and take photos of any scratches first.
stops.cost: About 150,000–200,000 VND (A$9–12) a day, so about A$30–36 for 3 days, plus fuel

stops.details: White sand and calm water on the southeast coast.

commute.label: Scooter two-up (25 km, main road south)

stops.cost: Free; sunbeds about 50,000–100,000 VND or buy food and drinks

stops.details: Leave the scooter at the resort tonight.
Mediterranean-style town with the Kiss Bridge for sunset.

commute.label: Taxi south (dark ride home and drinks, so no scooter)

stops.details: A regular sit-down restaurant in Sunset Town, not a festive set menu. Book ahead.
stops.bookLabel: Book with the restaurant or resort

stops.details: Night show on the water off Sunset Town: fountains, lasers, projections and fireworks. Book seats ahead and check the night's start time.
stops.hours: Usually one show a night, about 8:30 pm

title: Friday 25 December: Christmas Day
sub: Sleep in: Phu Quoc resort. Sunny, about 30°C.

stops.details: Most resorts do a special spread.
Totally free morning.
Or ride the scooter to a beach café nearby.
Stilt houses, a long wooden pier out over the sea and fresh crab and sea urchin straight from the boats.
On the beach.
A good restaurant near the resort instead of the pricey festive buffet. Book ahead.

title: Saturday 26 December: north Phu Quoc by scooter
sub: Sleep in: Phu Quoc resort. Sunny, about 30°C. Matthew rides the rented scooter with Amy on the back all day instead of taking taxis.

stops.details: Fill the tank (about 50,000 VND) and put water and sunscreen under the seat.
Open-range safari park. Leave the scooter in the car park.

commute.label: Scooter two-up north (30 km, main road)

stops.cost: About 650,000 VND (A$40); combo with VinWonders costs more

stops.hours: Open all day; light shows in the evening

stops.details: Short stop and tasting; Phu Quoc is famous for pepper.
stops.cost: Free; buy pepper if you like

stops.details: Shallow water with starfish; look, don't lift. The last stretch is a quieter rural road.
Shower and change. Return the scooter tonight or before checkout tomorrow.
Seafood grilled to order. Pick busy stalls with hot, fresh food.
stops.cost: Free entry; seafood about A$15–30 each

title: Sunday 27 December: fly to Bangkok
sub: Sleep in: Bangkok (Bang Rak, by the river). Dry, coolest month, 22 to 32°C.

stops.details: Thailand Digital Arrival Card should already be done.
Direct if scheduled, otherwise via Saigon. Same time zone.
Unpack and unwind after the flight.
Pad thai and mango sticky rice nearby.

stops.what: Grand Palace and Wat Phra Kaew
stops.details: Go at opening. Covered shoulders and knees.

commute.label: Chao Phraya Express Boat to Tha Chang

stops.hours: 8:30 am – 3:30 pm daily (ticket office closes 3:30 pm)

stops.details: The 46 m reclining Buddha.
Climb the steep prang for river views.
Rest through the hottest part of the day.
Tiny old riverside quarter: crumbling Chinese shophouses, lanes stacked with old car parts, street art, shrines and hidden cafés. Best in the golden hour.
Street food after dark, then mango sticky rice.
stops.hours: Street food about 5 pm–midnight (quieter on Mondays)

stops.details: The Buddha head in the tree roots.
Three restored chedis, the old royal temple.
A local speciality.
Best in the late afternoon light.
Shower and a rest after the day out.

Bangkok's most-filmed night market: rows of lit-up tents, the giant volcano pork ribs and seafood cooked to order. Pick busy stalls cooking to order; the Esplanade mall nearby has sit-down restaurants too.
Morning walk; watch the monitor lizards.
Teak houses and silk; guided tours run all day.

commute.label: BTS Sala Daeng to National Stadium

stops.hours: 10 am – 6 pm daily, guided tours only

stops.details: Great food hall.
Riverside mall with an indoor floating market.

commute.label: BTS to Saphan Taksin, then free shuttle boat

stops.details: Rooftop lounge on the 32nd floor of the Millennium Hilton, right by ICONSIAM. River views at sunset (about 5:50 pm).
stops.cost: No entry fee; cocktails about 400–550 THB (A$18–25)

stops.details: Riverside night market and sit-down restaurants.

commute.label: Hilton boat to Sathorn pier, then free Asiatique shuttle boat

title: Thursday 31 December: New Year's Eve in Bangkok

stops.details: Sleep in; it's a late night.
Climb to the top of the white stupa for a glass pagoda under a glowing green ceiling painted with the universe. Free.
Back at the hotel before the late night.

stops.what: NYE riverside dinner and midnight fireworks
stops.details: Dinner at a riverside restaurant near ICONSIAM (book ahead), then watch one of Bangkok's biggest fireworks shows from the riverfront for free. Get a spot by about 9 pm; it gets very crowded.

commute.label: Grab to ICONSIAM (leave early, roads close)

stops.hours: Fireworks at midnight; be in place by about 9 pm
stops.cost: Fireworks free; dinner about A$40–80 each

title: Friday 1 January: Mae Klong train market and Amphawa
sub: Sleep in: Bangkok. Dry, 22 to 32°C. A private car for the afternoon and evening (Amphawa only runs Friday to Sunday).

stops.details: Late night, so a slow start.
Stalls pull back their awnings and baskets seconds before the train creeps through the market. A train usually arrives around 2:30 pm; check the day's times.

commute.label: Private driver to Samut Songkhram (80 km)

stops.hours: Trains usually about 8:30 am, 11:10 am, 2:30 pm and 5:40 pm

stops.details: Old wooden shophouses along the canal, food boats and grilled seafood. Liveliest from late afternoon.
Long-tail boat along the canals after dark to see fireflies glowing in the trees.
stops.cost: About 60–100 THB (A$3–5) a seat on a shared boat

title: Saturday 2 January: Chatuchak, Golden Mount and a last night out

stops.details: Saturdays and Sundays only. Go in the morning while it's cooler and pick a few sections.
stops.hours: Sat and Sun about 9 am – 6 pm

stops.details: Sit-down cafés inside the market.
Gentle climb of about 300 steps to a golden chedi with views over old Bangkok. Lovely at sunset.
A nice riverside restaurant to finish the trip.

title: Sunday 3 January: fly home from Bangkok
sub: Amy back to Hong Kong, Matthew back to Sydney, both on direct flights. Both at work Monday 4 January.

stops.details: Direct, about 2h40. A 1:30 pm flight lands around 5:10 pm Hong Kong time.
Direct (Thai Airways or Qantas), about 9 hours. A 2 pm flight lands around 3 am Monday Sydney time; an evening flight lands around 8 am, which is tight before work.
